A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, determine which represented billed revenue is tied to counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with source identifiers and association disposition.

universe_scope.source_constraint: Authoritative files in this data room only; no external knowledge.
entities_in_scope: counterparties named on invoices and contracts
exclusions: expired statements of work (not treated as active contracts)
revenue or contracts outside the data room

required_output_shape.field_provenance: Report invoice_id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status, and contract_id as they appear in sources.

world_true: Invoice records exist with billed amounts, currency, period, and status.
Contract documents exist with identifiable counterparties and textual terms.
Contract temporal status (e.g., whether a statement of work has expired) is a source-grounded fact.
Presence or absence of specific contractual clauses in contract text is a source-grounded fact.
purpose_policy: Acquisition-relevant condition: a contractual term that (a) requires consent or notice on change of control, (b) permits termination upon change of control, or (c) requires consent or notice before assignment (including assignment restricted except to affiliates, or assignment prohibited to a competitor).
Active contract: excludes expired statements of work per purpose policy.
Qualifying invoice: represented billed revenue whose counterparty has an active contract containing at least one acquisition-relevant condition.
Association disposition asserted vs unresolved (see epistemic_requirements).

epistemic_requirements: Missing identity linkage is not a negative contractual finding.
If a billed name and a contract counterparty cannot be confidently associated, record association as unresolved rather than omitting the invoice or asserting a join.
Asserted association requires confident linkage between billed party and contract counterparty.
Contractual clause classification (acquisition-relevant or not) must be grounded in contract text, not inferred from absence of identity.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Invoice is in scope for reporting but invoice-to-contract counterparty linkage cannot be made confidently.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Every invoice that qualifies under purpose policy (represented billed revenue with acquisition-relevant active-contract exposure, or exposure blocked only by unresolved identity) appears in invoices.
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: Each reported invoice includes all schema fields; source identifiers and amounts are not silently dropped.
completeness_expectations.negative_findings: Do not emit closed-world negatives for missing identity or unasserted joins; use unresolved association instead.
completeness_expectations.output_artifact: Single JSON file at purpose_ir/a/output.json matching schema.

purpose_specific_policies: Acquisition-relevant conditions are defined solely by the three enumerated clause families in visible_a.md.
An expired statement of work is never an active contract for this purpose.
Do not treat missing identity as evidence that no acquisition-relevant clause applies.
Do not write a prose memo; output JSON only.
Disposition mapping is purpose-local: only asserted and unresolved association values are permitted (no distinct/false join outcome in this schema).

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, reconcile customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, state whether it is confidently the same legal counterparty as another record, confidently distinct, or unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: Authoritative files in this data room only.
universe_scope.entities_in_scope: Every commercially relevant name or record needed to connect CRM accounts, billed names, governing contracts, and candidate registry legal entities.

required_output_shape.ordering: Sort links by left ascending, then right ascending.

world_true: Source records exist in CRM, billing, registry, and contract files with the identifiers and names given in sources.
Pairwise comparisons are between specific referents drawn from those systems, not abstract merged entities.
purpose_policy: SAME_ENTITY: confident judgment that two records denote the same legal counterparty.
DISTINCT: confident judgment that two records denote different legal counterparties.
UNRESOLVED: identification cannot be made confidently; absence of SAME_ENTITY is not equivalent to DISTINCT.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical sameness.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
Global merge on string similarity alone is prohibited.

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
Permit explicit unresolved identity; missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (distinct) judgment.
DISTINCT requires positive evidence of separateness, not default from unresolved pairs.
Links must use the prescribed identifier forms so downstream purposes can join on stable referent strings.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Pairwise identity between left and right referents cannot be confidently resolved to SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT.

completeness_expectations.link_coverage: Include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship.
completeness_expectations.pair_orientation: Each link is an oriented pair (left, right); completeness is over the required link set, not over all possible pairs in the Cartesian product.
completeness_expectations.output_artifact: Single JSON file at purpose_ir/b/output.json matching schema and identifier conventions.

purpose_specific_policies: Identifier rendering conventions are normative for this purpose and for purpose C cross-references.
Mechanical normalization of exact legal-form variants is allowed; fuzzy name matching is not sufficient for SAME_ENTITY.
Do not write a prose memo; output JSON only.
This purpose owns identity judgments; purposes A and C consume them but do not redefine identity thresholds.

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under the purpose-defined two-part test, or mark dependency unresolved when required identity joins are unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: Authoritative files in this data room only.
exclusions: expired contracts (do not create current dependency)
one-off paid historical invoices without an active contract

required_output_shape.ordering: Sort dependencies by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row.

world_true: Invoice open/closed (or equivalent) status as recorded in billing sources.
Contract text contains exclusivity, auto-renewal, or rolling-term provisions.
Contract active vs expired status from source documents and dates.
Which invoices and contracts refer to which named counterparties in sources.
purpose_policy: Commercially dependent counterparty: both (1) a current commercial relationship holds, and (2) the active contract contains at least one obligation kind from {exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term}.
Current commercial relationship: an open invoice, OR an active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term.
Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
A one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not establish current dependency.
status dependent vs unresolved is a purpose output disposition, not a world negation.

epistemic_requirements: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved (per purpose B or local linkage), report status as unresolved rather than dependent or as false/non-dependent.
Dependency rows aggregate contract_id, open_invoice_ids, and obligation_kinds only when joins are sufficiently grounded; otherwise emit unresolved.
Counterparty identifiers must follow purpose B forms (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:).

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Dependency cannot be asserted because required invoice–contract–counterparty identity or relationship linkage is unresolved.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Report a dependency row for each contract–counterparty combination that is either purpose-dependent or blocked solely by unresolved identity/linkage required for the two-part test.
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: Each row includes counterparty, contract_id, open_invoice_ids (possibly empty when unresolved), obligation_kinds (sorted subset of vocabulary), and status.
completeness_expectations.cross_purpose_dependency: Identity unresolved states from purpose B must propagate here; do not close the world by omitting unresolved rows.
completeness_expectations.output_artifact: Single JSON file at purpose_ir/c/output.json matching schema.

purpose_specific_policies: Two-part dependency test is conjunctive: current relationship AND qualifying obligation kind on an active contract.
obligation_kinds values are drawn only from exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term (sorted).
Reuse purpose B identifier forms; do not invent alternate counterparty keys.
Do not write a prose memo; output JSON only.
Unresolved identity is not equivalent to not dependent; emit unresolved status explicitly.
